Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 47, verse 1–12:

Madaniyya (Medinan), and it has thirty-eight verses, thirty-nine words, and two thousand three hundred and forty-nine letters.

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Ahmad al-Farisi informed us, by my reading to him: Abu 'Umar and Isma'il ibn Majid ibn Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami informed us: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Bushaykhi informed us: Sa'id ibn Hafs narrated to us, saying: I read to Ma'qil ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat Muhammad, it is incumbent upon Allah, exalted is He, to give him to drink from the rivers of Paradise" [16] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/159.]].

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿Those who disbelieve and bar others from the way of Allah — He will waste their deeds.﴾ Meaning: He nullified them and did not accept them. Al-Dahhak said: He nullified their plotting and scheming against the Prophet (ﷺ), and made their stratagem turn against them.

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, and believe in what has been sent down upon Muhammad — and it is the truth from their Lord — He will remove from them their misdeeds and set right their condition (bal)﴾: their state; its plural is "balat." Sufyan al-Thawri said: "and believe in what has been sent down upon Muhammad" — they did not oppose him in anything. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Those who disbelieve and bar" refers to the people of Makkah; "those who believe and do righteous deeds" refers to the Ansar.

﴿That is because those who disbelieve follow falsehood﴾ — meaning the devils; ﴿and that those who believe follow the truth from their Lord﴾ — meaning the Qur'an. ﴿Thus Allah sets forth for the people their parables﴾ — Allah makes clear to people. ﴿Their parables (amthalahum)﴾ — their forms (ashkalahum).

﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve (from the people of war), then strike the necks (al-riqab)﴾ — the necks, singular "raqabah." "Fa-darb" is in the accusative as an incitement. ﴿Until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them (athkhantumuhum)﴾ — meaning you have overcome them, subdued them, and they have become captives in your hands. ﴿Then bind them firmly (fa-shuddu al-watha')﴾ — lest they escape from you and flee. ﴿Then either grant freedom (mannan) after the captivity, by releasing them without compensation or ransom.﴾

﴿Or ransom (fida'an)﴾ — in the accusative by an implied verb; its meaning: either you grant them freedom, or you ransom them. The scholars differed concerning the ruling of this verse. A group said: it is abrogated by His saying: ﴿So if you encounter them in war, then disperse those behind them﴾ [[Surat al-Anfal: 57.]] ... the verse, and His saying: ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [[Surat al-Tawbah: 5.]]. This view was held by Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj, and it is a narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

Aqil ibn Muhammad informed us that Abu al-Faraj al-Baghdadi informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, who said: Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) was written to concerning a captive who had been taken, and it was mentioned that they sought his release for such-and-such ransom. Abu Bakr said: "Kill him; the killing of a man from the polytheists is more beloved to me than such-and-such."

Others said: it is muhkam (not abrogated), and the imam has the choice between killing, granting freedom, and ransom. This is the view of Ibn 'Umar, al-Hasan, and 'Ata', and it is the preferred opinion, because the Prophet (ﷺ) and the rightly-guided caliphs did all of that.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) killed 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith on the day of Badr, by way of execution (sabran), and he ransomed the rest of the captives of Badr.

It was also said: (this was done) regarding Banu Qurayzah, who had come down under the judgement of Sa'd, and became in his hand as a peace-offering; and he granted freedom to Thumamah ibn Uthal al-Hanafi while he was a captive in his hand.

Aqil informed us that Abu al-Faraj al-Qadi al-Baghdadi informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from a man from the people of Syria who used to guard 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, who said: "I never saw 'Umar kill a captive except one man from the Turks. Captives from the Turks were brought, and he ordered that they be enslaved. A man among those who had brought them said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, if you had seen this one (one of them) killing Muslims, you would have wept much over them.' 'Umar said: 'He has been ransomed (qad fadaka), so kill him.' So he stood up and killed him."

﴿Until the war lays down its burdens (awzarahā)﴾ — its loads and its burdens, so that there is no more war. It was also said: until the war lays down its sins and its crimes, so that it is lifted and ends, for war is never free of sin on one side or the other. It was also said: its meaning is until the people of war lay down their equipment and their gear (or their weapons), and cease fighting.

"Al-harb" (war) means the fighting people, like "al-shurb" and "al-rakb." It was also said: until the warring enemies lay down their burdens and sins by repenting from their disbelief and believing in Allah and His Messenger. "Awzar" is also said of the horses (kura'): the Poet al-A'sha said:

"I prepared for war its burdens: long spears and male horses."

The meaning of the verse: inflict slaughter upon the polytheists by killing and capture until Islam prevails over all religions, and every people enter it willingly or unwillingly, ﴿and religion be entirely for Allah﴾ [[Surat al-Anfal: 39.]], so that there is no need for fighting and jihad; and that will be at the descent of 'Isa (peace be upon him).

Al-Hasan said: its meaning is until none is worshipped but Allah. Al-Kalbi said: until they accept Islam or make peace.

﴿That (is the ruling) which I have mentioned and explained concerning the disbelievers. And had Allah willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them﴾ — He would have destroyed them and sufficed you against them without fighting.

﴿But (He wills) to test some of you by means of others﴾ — concerning the ruling on the disbelievers, ﴿and that We may know those among you who strive and who are steadfast...﴾

﴿And those who were killed in the way of Allah﴾: al-Hasan read "qutilu" with a damma on the qaf and a kasra on the ta' with shaddah, without alif; Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub and Hafs read with a damma on the qaf and a kasra on the ta' with no shaddah, without alif, and Abu Hatim chose this reading, meaning "the martyrs." 'Asim al-Jahdari read "qatalu" with a fatha on the qaf and the ta', without alif, meaning "and those who killed the polytheists." The rest read "qatalu" (with an alif), from fighting (al-muqatalah), meaning the strivers (al-mujahidun), and Abu 'Ubayd chose this reading. ﴿He will never let their deeds be lost.﴾

Qatadah said: it was mentioned to us that this verse was revealed on the day of Uhud, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in the mountain pass, and wounds and killing had spread among them. The polytheists had called out: "Hubal is exalted!" The Muslims called out: "Allah is higher and more majestic!" The polytheists called out: "A day for a day, and war is a matter of turns; we have al-'Uzza and you have no 'Uzza!"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say: Allah is our Protector and you have no protector." [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/58.]] — for the battles are varied: as for our slain, they are "alive with their Lord, provided for" (Surat Al 'Imran: 169), and as for your slain, they are in the Fire, being punished.

﴿He will guide them﴾ in this world to obedience, and in the hereafter to the ranks.

﴿And He will set right their condition﴾ — He will satisfy their adversaries and accept their deeds. ﴿And will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾ — meaning He made clear to them their dwellings therein, so that they are guided to their homes and their ranks which Allah has apportioned to them; they do not err, nor does anyone need to guide them to them, as if they were its residents since they were created. A man comes to his dwelling therein when he enters it as he used to come to his dwelling in this world, with no confusion about it, and his guidance to his rank, his wife, his servants, and his blessings is more complete than his guidance to his family and home in this world. This is the view of most exegetes. Al-Mu'arrikh said: it means its fragrance; "al-'arf" is a pleasant scent. The Arabs say: "'arrafa al-marqah" when they season the broth with salt and spices. The poet said:

"And hands dip into throats (of camels) whose necks have been made to stretch for their customary broth, seasoned (al-muʿarraf)."

﴿O you who believe, if you support Allah﴾ — meaning His Messenger and His religion.

﴿He will support you and make firm your feet﴾ — upon Islam, and in fighting. ﴿But those who disbelieve — for them is ruin (fa-ta'san lahum)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "destruction for them." Abu al-'Aliyah said: "a fall." Al-Dahhak said: "loss." Ibn Zayd said: "wretchedness." Ibn Jarir said: "grief." Al-Farra' said: it is in the accusative as a verbal noun in the manner of supplication. The root of "ta'as" is in people and animals: it is said to one who stumbles, "ta'san," when they do not want him to rise; and it is said "atasahu Allah," so he is "ta'is" and "mut'is." Its opposite is "la'a," said when they want him to rise. Al-A'mash gathered them in one verse describing his she-camel:

"With a she-camel that stumbles, we forgive her when she trips; so 'ta'as' is closer to her than my saying 'la'a'."

﴿And He will waste their deeds﴾ — because they were in obedience to Satan, devoid of faith. ﴿That is the destruction and the distancing﴾. ﴿Because they disliked what Allah sent down, so He made their deeds fruitless.﴾ ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth and looked at how was the end of those before them?﴾ ﴿Allah destroyed them﴾ — meaning He annihilated them and destroyed their dwellings upon them; then He threatened the polytheists of Quraysh. ﴿And for the disbelievers are the like thereof﴾ if they do not believe. ﴿That (which I have mentioned and done) is because Allah is the Protector (mawla) of those who believe — their guardian, helper and keeper; and in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "That is because Allah is the Walī of those who believe."

﴿And that the disbelievers have no protector.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow.﴾ ﴿And those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat﴾ — their concern is only their bellies and their private parts, and they are heedless of what is ahead of them. It was also said: the believer in this world provides for the hereafter, the hypocrite adorns himself, and the disbeliever enjoys himself.

﴿And the Fire is their abode.﴾

It is also said: the man became asin (with kasra on the sin only), meaning he was struck by a foul wind and lost consciousness. Zuhayr said:

*He leaves the horn-bearer yellowed, as if he had been struck by a stench,*

Ladhdh and ladhidh are like tabb and tabib (similar forms with the same root). ﴿And rivers of purified honey﴾. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: The Tigris is the river of the Garden's water, the Euphrates is the river of its milk, the Nile of Egypt is the river of its wine, and the Sayhan is the river of its honey. These four rivers flow out of the river al-Kawthar.

﴿For them therein is every kind of fruit, and forgiveness from their Lord﴾. Is this like one who abides forever in the Fire? That is, the righteous, who are the people of the Garden, [are not like one who abides forever in the Fire]. The second part is omitted because the context indicates it. Ibn Kaysan said: The likeness of the Garden, in which are these rivers and fruits, is like the likeness of the Fire, in which is boiling water. The people of the Garden in everlasting bliss are like the people of the Fire in painful torment.

﴿And they are given boiling water to drink, which cuts their bowels to pieces﴾. When it is brought near them, it scorches their faces, and their scalps fall off. When they drink it, it cuts their intestines.

﴿And among them﴾, that is, among these disbelievers, ﴿are those who listen to you﴾, and they are the hypocrites, who listen to your words but do not understand or comprehend them, out of contempt and heedlessness. ﴿Until, when they leave you, they say to those who have been given knowledge﴾, from among the Companions, ﴿"What did he just say?"﴾ (ānifan means "just now," and its origin is "beginning").

Muqatil said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was delivering a sermon and urging the hypocrites. The hypocrites heard his words, and when they left the mosque they asked Abdullah ibn Mas'ud what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said, mocking and treating his words with contempt.

Ibn 'Abbas said concerning His words ﴿to those who have been given knowledge﴾: I am among them, and I have been asked among those who were asked. Qatadah said: These are the hypocrites. Two men entered: one understood from Allah and benefited from what he heard, and the other did not understand from Allah and gained nothing from what he heard. It was said: People are of three kinds: the listener who understands, the listener who acts, and the listener who is heedless and abandons.

﴿These are those upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal﴾, so they did not believe, ﴿and they followed their desires﴾. ﴿But as for those who are guided﴾, that is, the believers, ﴿He increases them in guidance and grants them their piety﴾, that is, He inspires them with it and grants them success. Ibn Mas'ud and al-A'mash recited wa-ātāhum (and granted them) as wa-anṭāhum, meaning "and gave them." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿and granted them the reward of their piety﴾.

It was also said: its proofs and evidences that it will occur. Its singular is shart. The root meaning of ashrāt is "markers." From it comes shart (condition), because they made for themselves a sign by which they would be recognized, and from it comes the shart in a sale and other transactions.

It is said: he made a condition for himself (ashratu nafsahu) in such-and-such a work, meaning he marked himself out and made himself a sign. Aws ibn Hajar described a man who had let himself down by a rope from the top of a mountain to a nabi'a tree in order to cut it and make a bow from it:

*He made himself a condition in it, and he was clinging, and he cast down his ropes and put his trust.* [[Gharib al-Hadith 1/41.]]

﴿How then will they have their reminder when it comes to them?﴾, that is, from where will they have remembrance, admonition, and repentance when the Hour comes upon them? A parallel is His words: ﴿And how can they reach it from a distant place?﴾ [[Surah Saba' 52.]]

Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya al-Kinani said: The Prophet (ﷺ) would become distressed and his chest would tighten because of the attacks of the disbelievers and the hypocrites against him, so Allah revealed this verse, meaning: know that there is no one who removes what troubles you except Allah, so do not attach your heart to anyone other than Him.

Abu al-'Aliyah and Ibn 'Uyaynah said: This is connected to what precedes it. Its meaning is: know that there is no refuge and no place of safety at the establishment of the Hour except Allah. I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Adash say: its meaning is that there is no judge on that Day except Allah. A parallel is ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾. [[Surah al-Fatihah 4.]]

﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾, so that he may set an example for his community through his Sunnah. It was also said: ﴿and ask forgiveness for your sin﴾ for the shortcoming that befell you in knowing Allah.

﴿And for the believing men and the believing women.﴾

Aqil ibn Muhammad informed us that Abu al-Faraj al-Qadi informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Abu Kurayb told us, 'Uthman ibn Sa'id told us, Ibrahim ibn Sulayman told us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Abdullah ibn Sarkhas, who said: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "May Allah forgive you, O Messenger of Allah." Then he recited: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and the believing women.﴾

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has no wealth with which to give charity, let him ask forgiveness for the believing men and the believing women, for it is a charity." [20] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id 10/21.]]

﴿And Allah knows your movement (mutaqallabakum) and your resting place (mathwakum).﴾ 'Ikrimah said: mutaqallabakum means your turning from the loins of fathers to the wombs of mothers, and mathwakum means your station on the earth. Ibn Kaysan said: mutaqallabakum means from back to belly, and mathwakum means your station in the graves. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak said: mutaqallabakum means your going and dispersing in your works in this world, and mathwakum means your return to the Garden or to the Fire. Ibn Jarir said: mutaqallabakum means your going about your business during the day, and mathwakum means your lying down to sleep at night. Nothing of this is hidden from Him.

﴿And those who believe say: "If only a surah were sent down!"﴾ out of longing for revelation and eagerness for jihad, meaning: if only a surah commanding us to fight were sent down. ﴿But when a decisive surah is sent down﴾ with commands and prohibitions, and in it fighting is mentioned, Qatadah said: every surah in which jihad is mentioned is a decisive surah, and it is the hardest for the hypocrites. He said: ﴿obedience﴾ (ṭā'atun), its meaning is: [they say] obedience, and it is in the nominative as a quotation, meaning "our matter is obedience" or "from us is obedience." ﴿But when the matter is resolved﴾, that is, when the matter is taken seriously and they are commanded to fight. ﴿If they had been true to Allah in showing faith and obedience, it would have been better for them.﴾ ﴿Then, is it likely that if you turn away﴾, that is, turn away from faith and from the Qur'an and depart from its rulings, ﴿you would cause corruption on the earth﴾ through disobedience, oppression, and bloodshed, and return to what you were upon in the time of ignorance, of division, after Allah had united you through Islam and honored you with fellowship.

Qatadah said: How did you see those people when they turned away from the Book of Allah? Did they not shed forbidden blood, sever the ties of kinship, and disobey the Merciful?

Some said: this is part of the verse. Al-Musayyab ibn Sharik and al-Farra' said: its meaning is: ﴿Is it likely that if you turn away﴾, if you take charge of people's affairs, ﴿you would cause corruption on the earth﴾ through injustice. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun told us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, al-Qasim ibn Yunus al-Hilali told us, from Sa'id ibn al-Hakam al-Warraq, from Ibn Dawud, from Abdullah ibn Mughaffal, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) recite: "Is it likely that if you turn away you would cause corruption on the earth," and then he said: "They are this clan of Quraysh. Ali ibn Abi Talib recited: in tuwuliytum, with a damma on the taʾ and the waw and a kasra on the lam, meaning: if they were governed by oppressive rulers, you would go out with them in strife and assist them. [[In Tafsir al-Tabari 6/483: "ay wuliya 'alaykum" (meaning, he was placed over you). In Tafsir al-Qurtubi: "harabtumuhum" (you fought against them).]]

Similar to this was narrated by Ruways from Ya'qub.

﴿And sever your ties of kinship.﴾ Ya'qub, Abu Hatim, and Salam recited wa-taqta'u (light), from qata' (cutting), taking as a model His words: ﴿And they sever what Allah has commanded to be joined﴾. [[Surah al-Baqarah 27.]] Al-Hasan recited taqattaʿū with the letters vowelled with fatha, taking as a model His words: ﴿So they divided their affair among themselves﴾. [[Surah al-Mu'minun 53.]] Others recited wa-tuqatti'u with a damma on the taʾ and with shadda, from taqti', for intensification on account of the ties of kinship.

Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya al-Kinani said: The Prophet (ﷺ) would become distressed and his chest would tighten because of the attacks of the disbelievers and the hypocrites against him, so Allah revealed this verse, meaning: know that there is no one who removes what troubles you except Allah, so do not attach your heart to anyone other than Him.

Abu al-'Aliyah and Ibn 'Uyaynah said: This is connected to what precedes it. Its meaning is: know that there is no refuge and no place of safety at the establishment of the Hour except Allah. I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Adash say: its meaning is that there is no judge on that Day except Allah. A parallel is ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾. [[Surah al-Fatihah 4.]]

﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾, so that he may set an example for his community through his Sunnah. It was also said: ﴿and ask forgiveness for your sin﴾ for the shortcoming that befell you in knowing Allah.

﴿And for the believing men and the believing women.﴾

Aqil ibn Muhammad informed us that Abu al-Faraj al-Qadi informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Abu Kurayb told us, 'Uthman ibn Sa'id told us, Ibrahim ibn Sulayman told us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Abdullah ibn Sarkhas, who said: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "May Allah forgive you, O Messenger of Allah." A man from the people said: "He asks forgiveness for you, O Messenger of Allah?!" He said: "Yes, and for you." [19]

Then he recited: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and the believing women.﴾

Ibn Manjuwayh al-Dinawari informed us, Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn 'Umar ibn Habash al-Razi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Ayyash al-'Utbi told us, Abu 'Uthman Sa'id ibn 'Anbasah al-Harrāz told us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad told us, from Bakr ibn Hunays, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Yahya ibn Wardan, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has no wealth with which to give charity, let him ask forgiveness for the believing men and the believing women, for it is a charity." [20] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id 10/21.]]

﴿And Allah knows your movement (mutaqallabakum) and your resting place (mathwakum).﴾ 'Ikrimah said: mutaqallabakum means your turning from the loins of fathers to the wombs of mothers, and mathwakum means your station on the earth. Ibn Kaysan said: mutaqallabakum means from back to belly, and mathwakum means your station in the graves. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak said: mutaqallabakum means your going and dispersing in your works in this world, and mathwakum means your return to the Garden or to the Fire. Ibn Jarir said: mutaqallabakum means your going about your business during the day, and mathwakum means your lying down to sleep at night. Nothing of this is hidden from Him.

﴿And those who believe say: "If only a surah were sent down!"﴾ out of longing for revelation and eagerness for jihad, meaning: if only a surah commanding us to fight were sent down. ﴿But when a decisive surah is sent down﴾ with commands and prohibitions, and in it fighting is mentioned, Qatadah said: every surah in which jihad is mentioned is a decisive surah, and it is the hardest for the hypocrites. In the reading of Abdullah it is "a new surah" (sūratun muhdatha). ﴿You see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning the hypocrites, ﴿looking at you with a glazed stare﴾ (shazran), that is, a fixed, intense gaze out of their hatred of jihad and their cowardice in facing the enemy, ﴿like the look of one who has fainted from death.﴾ ﴿Woe to them!﴾ is a threat and warning. He said: ﴿obedience﴾ (ṭā'atun), its meaning is: [they say] obedience, and it is in the nominative as a quotation, meaning "our matter is obedience" or "from us is obedience." These hypocrites would say, before the decisive verse was revealed: "Obedience."

﴿And a good word﴾, meaning a fair one. It was also said: this is connected to the first statement, and the lam in ﴿for them﴾ carries the meaning of the bā' (with/to), so its meaning is: obedience to Allah and His Messenger is better for them, and a good word, namely acceptance and obedience.

﴿But when the matter is resolved﴾, that is, when the matter is taken seriously and they are commanded to fight. ﴿If they had been true to Allah in showing faith and obedience, it would have been better for them.﴾ ﴿Then, is it likely that if you turn away﴾, that is, turn away from faith and from the Qur'an and depart from its rulings, ﴿you would cause corruption on the earth﴾ through disobedience, oppression, and bloodshed, and return to what you were upon in the time of ignorance, of division, after Allah had united you through Islam and honored you with fellowship.

Qatadah said: How did you see those people when they turned away from the Book of Allah? Did they not shed forbidden blood, sever the ties of kinship, and disobey the Merciful?

Some said: this is part of the verse. Al-Musayyab ibn Sharik and al-Farra' said: its meaning is: ﴿Is it likely that if you turn away﴾, if you take charge of people's affairs, ﴿you would cause corruption on the earth﴾ through injustice. It was revealed concerning the Banu Umayyah. The evidence for this interpretation is what

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun told us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, al-Qasim ibn Yunus al-Hilali told us, from Sa'id ibn al-Hakam al-Warraq, from Ibn Dawud, from Abdullah ibn Mughaffal, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) recite: "Is it likely that if you turn away you would cause corruption on the earth," and then he said: "They are this clan of Quraysh. Allah took a covenant from them that if they took charge of the people, they would not cause corruption on the earth nor sever their ties of kinship." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi 16/246.]]

Ali ibn Abi Talib recited: in tuwuliytum, with a damma on the taʾ and the waw and a kasra on the lam, meaning: if they were governed by oppressive rulers, you would go out with them in strife and assist them. [[In Tafsir al-Tabari 6/483: "ay wuliya 'alaykum" (meaning, he was placed over you). In Tafsir al-Qurtubi: "harabtumuhum" (you fought against them).]]

Similar to this was narrated by Ruways from Ya'qub.

﴿And sever your ties of kinship.﴾ Ya'qub, Abu Hatim, and Salam recited wa-taqta'u (light), from qata' (cutting), taking as a model His words: ﴿And they sever what Allah has commanded to be joined﴾. [[Surah al-Baqarah 27.]] Al-Hasan recited taqattaʿū with the letters vowelled with fatha, taking as a model His words: ﴿So they divided their affair among themselves﴾. [[Surah al-Mu'minun 53.]] Others recited wa-tuqatti'u with a damma on the taʾ and with shadda, from taqti', for intensification on account of the ties of kinship.

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He has made them deaf and blinded their eyes﴾, that is, to the truth.

Why do they not ponder the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts? (Muhammad 47:24)

The admonitions and rulings of the Qur'an. Akhbarana ʿAqil ibn Muhammad, akhbarana al-Muʿafa ibn Zakariyya, akhbarana Muhammad ibn Jarir, haddathana Ibn Humayd, haddathana Yahya ibn Wadih, haddathana Thawr ibn Yazid, from Khalid ibn Maʿdan, who said: No person is without four eyes:

Two eyes in his face, for his worldly life and his livelihood, and two eyes in his heart, for his religion and for what Allah has promised of the unseen. And no person is without a devil clinging to the base of his spine, bending his neck over his shoulder, his mouth agape toward the fruit of his heart. When Allah intends good for a servant, the two eyes in his heart see what Allah the Exalted has promised of the unseen, and he acts upon it. When Allah intends evil for a servant, He blinds those two eyes. That is His saying: "Or are there locks upon their hearts?"

And through the same chain, from Ibn Jarir: haddathana Bishr, haddathana Hammad ibn Zayd, haddathana Hisham ibn ʿUbayda, from his father, who said:

One day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: "Why do they not ponder the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?" A young man from the people of Yemen said: "Rather, there are locks upon them until Allah opens them or unlocks them." The young man remained in ʿUmar's mind until he was appointed and sought his help.

Indeed, those who turned back on their heels after guidance had become clear to them... (Muhammad 47:25)

Qatadah said: They are disbelievers among the People of the Book, who disbelieved in Muhammad while recognising him and finding his description written among them. Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: They are the hypocrites.

Satan has enticed them (Muhammad 47:25)... zayyana lahum: adorned it for them; and he gave them respite (Muhammad 47:25). Abu ʿAmr read wa-umliya (with the alif vowelled with a damma and the yaʾ with a fatha) in the passive form, without naming the agent. Mujahid and Yaʿqub read wa-umlī (with a damma on the alif and the yaʾ pronounced without a fatha, as the verb "amlā"), in the sense of a report from Allah the Exalted about Himself, that He does this to them. This is the choice of Abu Hatim. The rest read wa-amlā (with a fatha on the alif), meaning "Allah gave them respite," and this is the choice of Abu ʿUbayda.

That is because they (i.e., these hypocrites, or the Jews) said to those who hated what Allah had sent down (i.e., the polytheists): "We will obey you in part of the matter," in opposing Muhammad (ﷺ) and in holding back from jihad.

And Allah knows their secrets. The people of Kufa, except Abu Bakr, read "isrāruhum" with a kasra on the alif, as a verb. Others read it with a fatha, as the plural of "sirr" (secret).

How then, when the angels take their souls, striking their faces and their backs? The standard reading (ʿāmma) is "tawaffat-hum" with a taʾ. ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar read "tawaffī-hum" with a yāʾ. This is at death, and it has parallels in al-Anfal and al-Nahl. That is because they followed what displeased Allah and disliked His pleasure, so He nullified their deeds. (Muhammad 47:28)

Or do those in whose hearts is a disease, meaning the hypocrites, think that Allah will not bring forth their spite, meaning their grudges against the believers? Its singular is "dhaghn." He will expose it to them until they recognise their hypocrisy. And if We willed, We would have shown them to you, meaning: We would have made you know them, acquainted you with them, and pointed them out to you. The Arabs say: "I will show you what I will do," meaning "I will inform you," and from this is His saying: "by what Allah has shown you" (al-Nisa 4:105).

You would know them by their mark (Muhammad 47:30), by their sign.

Anas ibn Malik said: After the revelation of this verse, nothing of the hypocrites was concealed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He used to know them by their mark. We were with him on a military expedition, and among us were seven hypocrites whom people complained about. They slept one night, and in the morning each of them had written upon him: "This is a hypocrite."

That is His saying: "by their mark."

Ibn Zayd said: Allah intended to expose their hypocrisy, and commanded that they be removed from the mosque. They refused except to hold fast to "There is no god but Allah." When they refused to hold to anything but "There is no god but Allah," their blood was spared, and they married, and were married to.

And you will surely know them by the tone of their speech (Muhammad 47:30). Ibn ʿAbbas said: "In the meaning of the speech": its beauty in its import. Al-Qurazi said: its intent and its implication. "Lahn" has two senses: correct and erroneous. As for the correct sense, the verb from it is "lahana yalhanu lahnan," meaning "he became aware of a thing," and from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Perhaps some of you are more eloquent in his argument than others." The erroneous sense is also "lahana yalhanu lahnan," and the one who does it is "lāḥin," and its basic meaning is turning speech away from its proper course. It is reported that it was said to Muʿawiya: "ʿUbayd Allah ibn Ziyad speaks in Persian." He said: "Is it not a wonder from my nephew that he makes a mistake in his speech," meaning that he diverts it from one language to another. The poet said:

"A speech that is sound in logic, and at times it is pleasantly varied, and the best speech is that which is lahn." That is: its speech is measured.

And Allah knows your deeds. We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive and are patient, and We will test your reports (Muhammad 47:31). All the readers, except those cited in the next note, read it with a nun, based on His saying: "We would have shown them to you." Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal, from ʿAsim, read all of it with a yāʾ. Yaʿqub read "wa-nabluwa" with a silent waw, in response to His saying "naʿlama" (until We know).

Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath said: Al-Fudayl used to weep when he recited this verse, and say: "O Allah, do not test us, for if You test us You will tear down our coverings and disgrace us."

Indeed, those who disbelieved and barred from the way of Allah and opposed the Messenger after guidance had become clear to them, they will not harm Allah at all, and He will nullify their deeds (Muhammad 47:32). Ibn ʿAbbas said: They are those who fed others on the day of Badr. Its parallel is His saying: "Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to bar from the way of Allah" (al-Anfal 8:36), and so on.

O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and do not nullify your deeds (Muhammad 47:33) by disobeying them. Muqatil and al-Thumali said: Do not put Allah's Messenger under obligation, lest you nullify your deeds. It was revealed concerning the Banu Asad, and we will mention the story in Surat al-Hujurat, God willing. It was also said: by self-admiration and showing off.

Indeed, those who disbelieved and barred from the way of Allah, then died while they were disbelievers, Allah will not forgive them (Muhammad 47:34). It was said: they are the companions of the well (al-Qalib), and its ruling is general.

So do not weaken (Muhammad 47:35), do not lose strength, and do not call to peace, meaning reconciliation, while you are the superior ones (al-aʿlawn), because you are believers and in the right.

And Allah is with you. Qatadah said: Do not be the first of the two groups to submit to its companion. And He will not deprive you of your deeds (Muhammad 47:35). Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: He will not wrong you. Mujahid said: He will not diminish your deeds; rather, He will reward you for them and increase you from His bounty. From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever misses the afternoon prayer, it is as if he has lost his family and his wealth," meaning: has taken them away.

The life of this world is only play and amusement, but if you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards, and He will not ask you for your wealth (Muhammad 47:36). Your Lord does not ask you for wages; rather He commands you to believe and obey, so that He may reward you with Paradise. Its parallel is His saying: "I do not desire any provision from them" (al-Dhariyat 51:57), and so on. It was also said: "He will not ask you" means Muhammad asks you for a portion of your wealth as charity. Its parallel is His saying: "Say: I do not ask you for any wage for it" (Sad 38:86). It was also said: the meaning of the verse is that Allah and His Messenger do not ask you for all your wealth; they only ask a small part of it, a quarter of a tenth, so give it willingly. This view was taken by Ibn ʿUyayna, and it is the choice of Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbdash. He said: Ibn Habib related it to us from him, and the context of the verse supports it.

If He asks you for it and presses you (Muhammad 47:37), He will press you to exhaustion, insist upon you, and make you hard-pressed for it. Ibn Zayd said: al-ihfa' is that you take everything in your hand.

You would be stingy, and He would bring forth your spite (Muhammad 47:37). Qatadah said: Allah the Exalted knows that asking for wealth brings forth grudges.

Here you are, being called to spend in the way of Allah, yet among you is one who is stingy. And whoever is stingy is only stingy against himself. And Allah is the Rich, without need of your charity and obedience, and you are the poor in need of it. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be like you (Muhammad 47:38) in obedience. Rather, they will be more obedient to Allah the Exalted and better than you. al-Kalbi said: They are Kinda and al-Nakhaʿ. al-Hasan said: They are the non-Arabs (al-ʿAjam). ʿIkrima said: Persia and Rome.

Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Manjawayh al-Dinawari related to us: haddathana ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, haddathana ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Fadl, haddathana Yahya ibn Ayyub, haddathana Isma'il ibn Ja'far, akhbarani ʿAbd Allah ibn Najih, from al-ʿAla' ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: Some people among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are those whom Allah mentioned in the Qur'an, 'if we turn away they will replace us, and they will not be like us?'" He said: Salman was beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) struck the thigh of Salman and said: "This one and his people [in the source: 'his companions' instead of 'his people']. By Him in whose hand my soul is, if faith were suspended at the Pleiades, men from Persia would reach it" [in the source: 'would be attached' instead of 'suspended'].

And Allah is with you. Qatadah said: Do not be the first of the two groups to submit to its companion. And He will not deprive you of your deeds (Muhammad 47:35). Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: He will not wrong you. Mujahid said: He will not diminish your deeds; rather, He will reward you for them and increase you from His bounty. From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever misses the afternoon prayer, it is as if he has lost his family and his wealth," meaning: has taken them away.

The life of this world is only play and amusement, but if you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards, and He will not ask you for your wealth (Muhammad 47:36). Your Lord does not ask you for wages; rather He commands you to believe and obey, so that He may reward you with Paradise. Its parallel is His saying: "I do not desire any provision from them" (al-Dhariyat 51:57), and so on. It was also said: "He will not ask you" means Muhammad asks you for a portion of your wealth as charity. Its parallel is His saying: "Say: I do not ask you for any wage for it" (Sad 38:86). It was also said: the meaning of the verse is that Allah and His Messenger do not ask you for all your wealth; they only ask a small part of it, a quarter of a tenth, so give it willingly. This view was taken by Ibn ʿUyayna, and it is the choice of Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbdash. He said: Ibn Habib related it to us from him, and the context of the verse supports it.

If He asks you for it and presses you (Muhammad 47:37), He will press you to exhaustion, insist upon you, and make you hard-pressed for it. Ibn Zayd said: al-ihfa' is that you take everything in your hand.

You would be stingy, and He would bring forth your spite (Muhammad 47:37). Qatadah said: Allah the Exalted knows that asking for wealth brings forth grudges.

Here you are, being called to spend in the way of Allah, yet among you is one who is stingy. And whoever is stingy is only stingy against himself. And Allah is the Rich, without need of your charity and obedience, and you are the poor in need of it. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be like you (Muhammad 47:38) in obedience. Rather, they will be more obedient to Allah the Exalted and better than you. al-Kalbi said: They are Kinda and al-Nakhaʿ. al-Hasan said: They are the non-Arabs (al-ʿAjam). ʿIkrima said: Persia and Rome.

Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Manjawayh al-Dinawari related to us: haddathana ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, haddathana ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Fadl, haddathana Yahya ibn Ayyub, haddathana Isma'il ibn Ja'far, akhbarani ʿAbd Allah ibn Najih, from al-ʿAla' ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: Some people among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are those whom Allah mentioned in the Qur'an, 'if we turn away they will replace us, and they will not be like us?'" He said: Salman was beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) struck the thigh of Salman and said: "This one and his people [in the source: 'his companions' instead of 'his people']. By Him in whose hand my soul is, if faith were suspended at the Pleiades, men from Persia would reach it" [in the source: 'would be attached' instead of 'suspended'].
